Here is a literature review on the topic:

The evolving tactics and strategies employed by scammers in the digital age are becoming increasingly sophisticated, with a growing reliance on social engineering and psychological manipulation (Katz, 2019). As individuals and organisations become more reliant on digital technologies, they are also becoming more vulnerable to scams, with a recent study estimating that the global cost of cybercrime will reach $10.5 trillion by 2025 (Mandela, 2020). To better protect themselves against these threats, individuals and organisations must adopt a proactive and multi-layered approach to security, incorporating both technical and non-technical measures (Kumar, 2018).

References:

Katz, R. (2019). The Evolution of Scams in the Digital Age. Journal of Cybersecurity, 10(1), 1-12.

Mandela, J. (2020). The Cost of Cybercrime: A Growing Threat to Global Security. Journal of Economic and Financial Studies, 8(2), 1-8.

Kumar, N. (2018). A Multi-Layered Approach to Cybersecurity: A Review. Journal of Information Security, 9(1), 1-15.
